title: Integral Euler character of arbitrary flag line bundles
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, with these notions as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Use the character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and integer pairing of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$ as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Let $\lambda\in X$ be any character, with no dominance condition, and extend it to $\widetilde\lambda=\lambda\circ(B\to T)$. Let $Q=S/B$ and let $\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\lambda}$ be the homogeneous invertible sheaf of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], defined by $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\widetilde\lambda(b)z)$. Set $H^i=R^i\Gamma(Q,\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\lambda})$, the Zariski sheaf cohomology of this $\mathcal O_Q$-module. The natural left $S$-action on the line bundle induces rational $T$-actions on these finite-dimensional spaces; only finitely many $H^i$ are nonzero. For each $i$ there is a finite direct-sum decomposition $H^i=\bigoplus_{\eta\in X}H^i_\eta$, where $H^i_\eta$ consists of the vectors with coaction $v\mapsto v\otimes\eta$ for the restricted $T$-action. In the group algebra $\mathbf Z[X]$, the free abelian group on symbols $e^\eta$ with $e^\eta e^\xi=e^{\eta+\xi}$, define
$$q_\lambda=\sum_{i\ge0}(-1)^i\sum_{\eta\in X}(\dim_F H^i_\eta)e^\eta.$$
Let $W$ be the finite group of automorphisms of $X$ generated by the root reflections $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$, and set $A(\nu)=\sum_{w\in W}\det(w)e^{w\nu}$, with determinant on $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. Then
$$q_\lambda A(-\rho)=A(-\lambda-\rho)\quad\text{in }\mathbf Z[X].$$
All coefficients are ordinary integer dimensions, not their images in $F$, and the identity holds in every characteristic.

source.place: Section 22d, pp.479--480, Theorems 22.50--22.51, with signs corrected to the line-bundle definition in 18c and 22.48; Jantzen 2003 II.4.5 and II.5.10--5.12 are WANTED.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry to $G=S$; its hypothesis holds because lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure explicitly says that a semisimple group is reductive. It gives that $Q$ is smooth and projective, and that the fixed subscheme $Q^T$ is the disjoint union of the reduced points $p_w=n_wB$, indexed without repetition by $W_0=N_S(T)(F)/T(F)$, with tangent weights $\Phi\setminus w\Phi^+$ at $p_w$, each of multiplicity one. By lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice the simple roots form a $\mathbf Q$-basis of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, so the space $E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\Phi$ of lem-sfb-weyl-reflection-realization is all of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, and that lemma identifies $W_0$, acting on $X$ by $(w\eta)(t)=\eta(n_w^{-1}tn_w)$, with the group $W$ of the statement generated by the $s_\alpha$; it also says that $W$ permutes $\Phi$. Since $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup(-\Phi^+)$ and $w$ is linear and permutes $\Phi$, we get $\Phi\setminus w\Phi^+=-w\Phi^+$. The cotangent space is the dual representation, so its weights are the negatives: $w\alpha$ for $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, each once. These are nonzero characters, even in small characteristic.

Put $\chi=-\widetilde\lambda$. By lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections, $\mathcal L_\chi$ is an $S$-linearized invertible coherent sheaf with the specified quotient action. Compute its fibre character without changing conventions: $[n_wb,z]=[n_w,\chi(b)z]$, so for $t\in T$ we have $t[n_w,z]=[n_w(n_w^{-1}tn_w),z]=[n_w,\chi(n_w^{-1}tn_w)z]$. Its weight at $p_w$ is therefore $-w\lambda$. This is an identity after every $F$-algebra extension.

Apply lem-sfb-torus-coherent-fixed-point-formula with $H=S$, $Z=Q$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\lambda}$. Step 1 verifies smoothness, projectivity, the reduced finite fixed subscheme and its nonzero cotangent weights; step 2 verifies linearization and computes the fibre characters. The lemma gives all finite-dimensionality, vanishing and rational-action/weight-decomposition assertions in the item. Its integer Euler character is exactly the defined $q_\lambda$, and it gives
$$q_\lambda=\sum_{w\in W}\frac{e^{-w\lambda}}{\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{w\alpha})}\quad\text{in }\mathbf Z[X]_\Sigma.$$
No dominance, simplicity or vanishing theorem for dominant line bundles is being used.

source.place: 22.50, general fixed-point input; integral supporting formulation

proof.text:
The root-datum hypotheses of the denominator lemma (perfect integer pairing, finite reduced crystallographic root datum, $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2$, reflections permuting $\Phi$, positive system $\Phi^+$ with simple-root base $\Delta$) are the statement of lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure, and the spanning hypotheses hold for this semisimple simply connected group by lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice (the simple roots and coroots are bases of the respective rational spaces); $\rho\in X$ is already in the statement. Put $D=A(-\rho)$. By lem-sfb-root-datum-weyl-denominator, $D=e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha>0}(1-e^\alpha)$. Directly reindexing its defining finite sum gives $wD=\det(w)D$: set $u=wv$ and use $\det(v)=\det(w)\det(u)$. Applying $w$ to the product expression now gives
$$\prod_{\alpha>0}(1-e^{w\alpha})=\det(w)e^{w\rho}D.$$
The element $D$ is a unit in the same localization, since every root is nonzero and $e^{-\rho}$ is a unit.

source.place: Appendix C and 22d; explicit denominator manipulation

proof.text: Multiply the formula in step 3 by $D$ and substitute step 4 term by term. The $w$-term becomes $\det(w)e^{-w\lambda-w\rho}$. Summing gives $q_\lambda D=A(-\lambda-\rho)$ in the localization. Choose an integer basis of the finite-rank free lattice $X$; then $\mathbf Z[X]$ is the Laurent polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$ in those basis variables. Products of nonzero Laurent polynomials are nonzero (take a lexicographically largest exponent in each finite support). In particular every $1-e^\eta$ with $\eta\ne0$ is nonzero, and localization at their products is injective: an element mapping to zero is annihilated by a nonzero such product. Hence the equality already holds in $\mathbf Z[X]$. All coefficients stayed integers throughout. For rank zero the products and the single Weyl sum are $1$, and the same argument applies.
